The Season Finale

Twelve episodes. Countless cups of coffee. One very brave learner. Today we finish Season One — and open the door to what comes next. All in English, of course. ☕

This one's all about you.

~90 min total. Move through the six chapters with the rail on top or the Back/Next bar. Toggle these purple notes with the ☕ button — Veronika won't see them unless you switch them on. Fireflies (✦) are just for atmosphere. Suggested pacing: Warm-up 7′ · Victory Lap 30′ · Then & Now 10′ · Time Capsule 12′ · Chapter Two 12′ · Finale 10′.
Chapter One

How are you leaving this season?

No grammar yet — just talking. Draw a card, take your time, tell me the real answer.

🗣️ Speaking · ~7 min
Question 1 of 7
How are you feeling today — in three words?
Today I'm running on…
Let her lead. If she gives a one-word answer, smile and ask “why?” or “tell me more.” The mood row is a light way to start; you can mirror it (“me too, very ☕ today”). No corrections here — this is warm-up, build confidence.

Chapter Three

Then & Now

Rewind to Episode One. Look how far the character has come. Fill these in — say them out loud first, then type.

✍️ Speaking + writing · ~10 min
Episode 1
The Finale
Then
Now
Model the structures first: “Before, I couldn't… Now, I can…” / “I used to…, but now I…” This is gentle present-perfect + used to practice hiding inside a reflection. If she's stuck, remind her of a specific early lesson. Their answers here can feed straight into the Time Capsule next.
Chapter Four

The Time Capsule

Write a note to Future Veronika — the one who comes back to English in a while, a little more rested. Seal it, then save it as a real letter image to keep for later. This is yours to keep.

💌 Writing · ~12 min
✉
Ready when you are.
The emotional centre of the lesson — give it space. She can write in English at whatever level feels right; accuracy matters less than meaning here. The baby line is optional on purpose (keep the focus on her). After sealing, the Download button saves a beautifully formatted letter image she can keep on her phone or print later. Encourage that — it's the payoff.
Chapter Five

Chapter Two: a peek at B1

Think you're “only A2”? Watch this. Here's a task from the next level — and you're going to do it right now.

🚀 Reading + speaking · ~12 min
B1 · Read this

Maya closed her laptop and smiled. She had been studying English for two years, and tonight she finished her last class before a long break. She wasn't stopping forever — she was just resting. “I'll come back,” she thought, “and next time it will be even easier.” Outside, the city lights were coming on, one by one.

Talk to me (this is the B1 part 👀)
  • Why isn't Maya sad about stopping?
  • How do you think she'll feel when she comes back?
  • Are you a little bit like Maya right now? Why / why not?
Use these to sound extra B1:
I think that…In my opinion…She probably… One reason is…On the other hand…If I …, I will …
One-sentence challenge ⭐

Finish this out loud, then type it — it's a real B1 structure (first conditional):

You're ready for the next chapter.
We'll open it when you come back.

Don't pre-teach — let her try the reading cold, then be amazed she understood it. That surprise is the whole point of this chapter. The phrase bank is scaffolding; the conditional at the end is a clean, achievable B1 win to end on. Praise specifically (“that's a B1 sentence, full stop”).
